enrolled and randomized 1:1 to receive either isavuconazonium sulfate or voriconazole.

population.text: Patients ≥18 years of age with proven, probable, or possible invasive fungal disease per EORTC/MSG 2008 criteria; patients with creatinine clearance <50 mL/min were excluded.

citations.quote: Patients \ge 18 years of age with proven, probable, or possible invasive fungal disease (IFD) per the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer/My coses Study Group (EORTC/MSG) 2008 criteria2 were enrolled and randomized 1:1 to receive either isavuconazonium sulfate or voriconazole. Patients with renal impairment (creatinine clearance less than 50 mL/min) were excluded.

endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was all-cause mortality through Day 42; key secondary endpoint was DRC-assessed overall response at end of treatment.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was all-cause mortality through Day 42. A key secondary efficacy endpoint was the Data Review Committee (DRC) assessment of overall response at the end of treatment

n.text: 527 patients enrolled; ITT population of 516 (258 in each treatment group).

citations.quote: The trial enrolled 527 patients at 102 centers globally.
The ITT population consisted of 516 patients (258 in each treatment group).

result.text: In the ITT population, Day 42 all-cause mortality was 48/258 (18.6%) for isavuconazonium vs 52/258 (20.2%) for voriconazole; adjusted treatment difference -1.0 (95% CI -8.0, 5.9). As the upper bound of the 95% CI (ranging 5.9% to 8.2% across populations) was below the pre-specified NI margin of 10%, noninferiority was demonstrated.

citations.quote: The upper bounds of the 95% confidence interval (CI) around the adjusted treatment difference ranged from 5.9% to 8.2%. As the upper bound of the 95% CI was less than the pre-specified NI margin of 10%, noninferiority of isavuconazonium sulfate relative to voriconazole was demonstrated with respect to all-cause mortality through Day 42.

endpoint.text: DRC-assessed overall response was the protocol primary endpoint, but 42-day all-cause mortality was agreed by the Applicant and FDA as the most relevant primary endpoint to allow comparison with historical controls.

citations.quote: DRC-assessed overall response was specified as the primary endpoint in the protocol. result.text: In the mITT-Mucorales population, all-cause mortality at Day 42 was 38% and at Day 84 was 43%; 31% of patients were assessed as success (14% complete, 17% partial), compared with historical untreated mucormycosis mortality estimates up to 97%.

target_moa.text: Isavuconazole, the active moiety of the prodrug isavuconazonium sulfate, inhibits the enzyme cytochrome P450 sterol 14 alpha-demethylase (CYP51), interfering with ergosterol synthesis; ergosterol depletion disrupts fungal membrane structure and function, inhibiting fungal growth.

citations.quote: Similar to other azoles, isavuconazole acts by inhibiting the enzyme cytochrome P450 sterol 14 \alpha-demethylase, thereby interfering with the synthesis of ergosterol. Depletion of ergosterol disrupts the structure and function of the fungal membrane leading to inhibition of fungal growth.

key_safety.text: Across two clinical trials (403 patients), the most frequently reported adverse reactions were nausea (26%), vomiting (25%), diarrhea (22%), headache (17%), elevated liver chemistry tests (16%), hypokalemia (14%), constipation (13%), dyspnea (12%), cough (12%), peripheral edema (11%), and back pain (10%). Hepatic adverse drug reactions, infusion-related reactions, and hypersensitivity reactions are warnings in labeling.

citations.quote: A total of 403 patients were exposed to CRESEMBA in two clinical trials. The most frequently reported adverse reactions among CRESEMBA-treated patients were nausea (26%), vomiting (25%), diarrhea (22%), headache (17%), elevated liver chemistry tests (16%), hypokalemia (14%), constipation (13%), dyspnea (12%), cough (12%), peripheral edema (11%), and back pain (10%).

Hepatic adverse drug reactions, infusion-related reactions, hypersensitivity reactions, and the need to administer isavuconazonium sulfate through an in-line filter are included as warnings in the Warnings and Precautions section of the package insert.

detail.text: A REMS was determined not to be required; safety findings were considered adequately addressed in labeling.

summary.text: NDA 207500 was submitted by Astellas on July 8, 2014 for treatment of invasive aspergillosis and invasive mucormycosis. Isavuconazonium sulfate carried QIDP designation under GAIN, which granted priority review, and had orphan drug designation for both indications. Aspergillosis efficacy was shown in a randomized double-blind noninferiority trial versus voriconazole, while mucormycosis efficacy was supported by a single-arm open-label trial compared against historical controls; the drug was approved March 2015 as a standard (non-accelerated) approval.

citations.quote: NDA 207500 and 207501, isavuconazonium sulfate capsules and sterile lyophilized powder for injection respectively, were submitted by Astellas Pharma Global Development, Inc. on behalf of Astellas Pharma US, Inc. on July 08, 2014 for treatment of invasive aspergillosis and treatment of invasive mucormycosis.
